biological.citation: CUL3-KBTBD6/KBTBD7 ubiquitin ligase cooperates with GABARAP proteins to spatially restrict TIAM1-RAC1 signaling. (PMID: 25684205)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 (together with KBTBD6) acts as a substrate adaptor for a CUL3 RING ubiquitin ligase complex that mediates ubiquitylation and proteasomal degradation of TIAM1, a RAC1-specific GEF. Depletion of KBTBD6/7 leads to elevated RAC1 activity, actin morphology changes, loss of focal adhesions, reduced proliferation, and enhanced invasion. KBTBD6/7 use ATG8 family-interacting motifs to bind GABARAP proteins, and TIAM1 degradation depends on recruitment to GABARAP-containing vesicles, revealing a role in spatially restricted RAC1 signaling.

biological.citation: The KBTBD6/7-DRD2 axis regulates pituitary adenoma sensitivity to dopamine agonist treatment. (PMID: 32572597)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 was identified as a DRD2-interacting protein via yeast two-hybrid screening and shown to directly ubiquitinate DRD2 at five sites (K221, K226, K241, K251, K258) as a substrate adaptor for the CUL3-RING ubiquitin ligase complex. KBTBD7 knockout mice (generated by CRISPR-Cas9) showed elevated DRD2 protein levels in pituitary gland, thalamus, and heart. KBTBD7 was highly expressed in dopamine-resistant prolactinomas and its knockdown sensitized pituitary tumor cells to cabergoline treatment.

biological.citation: Regulation of Wnt/PCP signaling through p97/VCP-KBTBD7-mediated Vangl ubiquitination and endoplasmic reticulum-associated degradation. (PMID: 33990333)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 functions as an E3 ligase recruited by p97/VCP via UBA-UBX adaptors to promote ubiquitination and ERAD of Vangl1/Vangl2, core components of Wnt/planar cell polarity signaling. Wnt5a/CK1-induced Vangl phosphorylation prevents this KBTBD7-mediated degradation, allowing Vangl export to the plasma membrane. In vivo, KBTBD7 regulates convergent extension during zebrafish gastrulation and acts as a tumor suppressor in breast cancer by promoting Vangl degradation.

biological.citation: MicroRNA-21 prevents excessive inflammation and cardiac dysfunction after myocardial infarction through targeting KBTBD7. (PMID: 29991775)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 was identified as a direct target of miR-21 in macrophages; miR-21 deficiency enhanced DAMP-triggered inflammatory cytokine production (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α) and p38/NF-κB signaling, while miR-21 overexpression inhibited these responses. KBTBD7 was shown to interact with MKK3/6 and promote their activation, thereby enhancing downstream p38 and NF-κB signaling induced by DAMPs (HMGB1, HSP60). In miR-21 knockout mice, cardiac dysfunction, infarct size, and inflammatory infiltration were significantly worsened after MI.

biological.citation: KBTBD7 promotes non-small cell lung carcinoma progression by enhancing ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PTEN. (PMID: 35499228)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 was found to be highly expressed in NSCLC tissues (102 paired specimens) and cell lines, correlating with histological type, P-TNM stage, lymph node metastasis, and tumor size. KBTBD7 enhances ubiquitin-dependent degradation of PTEN, thereby activating EGFR/PI3K/AKT signaling and promoting NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion. Downregulation of KBTBD7 inhibited NSCLC cell proliferation and invasion, modulating downstream proteins including CCNE1, CDK4, P27, ZEB-1, and MMP-9.

biological.citation: New TFII-I family target genes involved in embryonic development. (PMID: 19527686)
biological.summary: Kbtbd7 (1110008P08Rik) was identified as dramatically downregulated in mouse embryos with targeted disruption of Gtf2i and Gtf2ird1 (TFII-I family transcription factors) by microarray analysis. Kbtbd7 encodes an adapter protein with BTB/POZ, BACK, and Kelch motifs and its expression pattern suggests a specific role in brain development and function. The Kbtbd7 promoter contains well-conserved TFII-I-binding consensus sites, suggesting it is a direct transcriptional target of TFII-I proteins relevant to Williams syndrome.

biological.citation: Targeting of ubiquitination and degradation of KLF15 by E3 ubiquitin ligase KBTBD7 regulates LPS-induced septic brain injury in microglia. (PMID: 39489209)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 was upregulated in microglia of a rat cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) septic brain injury model and in LPS-treated primary microglia. Co-immunoprecipitation confirmed that KBTBD7 directly interacts with KLF15 and catalyzes its ubiquitin-proteasome-mediated degradation, thereby promoting NLRP3 inflammasome and NF-κB signaling activation. Knockdown of KBTBD7 inhibited proinflammatory cytokine release and inflammasome activation, and KLF15 knockdown abolished this anti-inflammatory effect, establishing a KBTBD7-KLF15 signaling axis in septic brain injury.

biological.citation: Knockdown of KBTBD7 attenuates septic lung injury by inhibiting ferroptosis and improving mitochondrial dysfunction. (PMID: 38652964)
biological.summary: KBTBD7 was highly expressed in LPS-induced human alveolar epithelial cells and in a mouse septic lung injury model. KBTBD7 knockdown reduced inflammatory cytokine secretion, ROS production, ferroptosis, and mitochondrial dysfunction both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, KBTBD7 interacts with FOXA1 and promotes its expression, which indirectly inhibits SLC7A11 transcription, linking KBTBD7 to ferroptosis regulation.

biological.citation: Berberine reduces inflammation of human dental pulp fibroblast via miR-21/KBTBD7 axis. (PMID: 31837588)
biological.summary: In LPS-stimulated human dental pulp fibroblasts, KBTBD7 was upregulated while miR-21 was downregulated; luciferase reporter assays confirmed that miR-21 directly and negatively targets KBTBD7. Silencing of KBTBD7 or overexpression of miR-21 inhibited NF-κB signaling (reduced phospho-IKKα/β, phospho-NF-κB p65) and decreased IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α levels. Berberine treatment reduced KBTBD7 expression and inflammatory responses via the miR-21/KBTBD7/NF-κB axis.

biological.citation: A transcriptome-wide association study of uterine fibroids to identify potential genetic markers and toxic chemicals. (PMID: 36174000)
biological.summary: A transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) integrating GWAS data for uterine fibroids with expression quantitative trait loci data identified KBTBD7 as one of nine significant TWAS genes, including as a novel candidate causal gene for uterine fibroid susceptibility. Functional enrichment network analyses implicated the immune system process as a key pathway involving KBTBD7 and other TWAS genes in uterine fibroid pathogenesis.
